label: Oct 26–30, 2026
title: Black October hits the web as Meta’s cash burn hits AI stocks
deck: A wave of attacks on AI-found PHP flaws, dubbed Black October, knocked websites offline and lifted cybersecurity stocks about 6% Friday. A day earlier, Meta’s first cash outflow in over a decade sank chip and AI stocks. The S&P 500 slipped 0.5% and rests on its 100-day line near 7,605. Next: the Fed, Microsoft and Alphabet Wednesday, then GDP, PCE and Amazon Thursday.

tldr.label: What changed
tldr.text: Black October: attacks on AI-found PHP flaws knocked sites offline and lifted cyber stocks about 6% Friday. Meta’s cash outflow sank chips and AI; small caps and the equal-weight S&P rose.

tldr.label: What’s next
tldr.text: Fed decision Wednesday, with Microsoft and Alphabet after the close. GDP, PCE and Amazon Thursday. A hold is expected; December hike odds are near 80%.

tldr.label: Who’s buying
tldr.text: ARK bought about $27M of Meta on its drop day and sold Alphabet. Reps. Fields and Jackson disclosed Nvidia, TSMC and Datadog buys.

scorecard.outcome: Meta beat on revenue but showed its first cash outflow in over a decade as AI spending outran cash coming in; the stock fell about 7% Thursday and 9.4% on the week. Tesla’s profit fell 44%, yet the stock rose 4.9% on SpaceX merger talk.
Held. The S&P 500 got back above its 50-day with a 7,757 close on Oct 21, then slipped to 7,623.68 by Friday. The week’s low was 7,612, above 7,567.
No reopening. Iran claimed new ship strikes, front-month Brent settled at $116.72 Friday, a six-month high, and December hike odds stayed near 80%.

levels.name: S&P 500
levels.note: Lance Roberts notes the index is resting on its 100-day average near 7,605, right at the lower Bollinger band, with a MACD sell signal. He would use rallies into the 50-day near 7,702 to rebalance. Below 7,605 come the Sept 16 low near 7,564 and the 200-day near 7,293.

sectors.title: Telecom and Meta dragged, the average stock rose
sectors.deck: Eight of eleven sectors rose. Communication services fell 4.4% on Meta and a telecom selloff; energy and health care led, and chip stocks fell 3.1%.

flows.label: Equal-weight vs S&P 500
flows.note: A second week of the average stock beating the megacaps. The Russell 2000 rose 2.0%.

flows.label: Rotation since Oct 2
flows.note: Per the Bull Bear Report, equal-weight and large-cap value each gained 3.2% over the same stretch.

flows.label: Stretch readings
flows.note: Energy, staples and health care are the most overbought; tech, chips and communications are oversold but not yet at extremes.

flows.label: Cybersecurity stocks, Friday
flows.note: Palo Alto, Okta, Cloudflare, CrowdStrike and Zscaler rallied as the PHP attacks spread. Analysts expect more spending on patching and monitoring.

sectors.takeaway: Selling is still concentrated in AI spenders and the names that supply them. Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon will show whether Meta’s cash squeeze is a one-off or a pattern.

news.headline: Black October: AI-found PHP flaws hit the web
news.body: Two critical PHP flaws found with AI help were patched Oct 21 and quickly exploited; PHP runs about 70% of websites. CISA urged patching or taking systems offline, and government sites in the US, UK and Europe went down to patch. Cloudflare’s CEO counted millions of exploit attempts within hours. Cyber stocks jumped Friday: Palo Alto +6.6%, Okta +6.3%, CrowdStrike +6.0%.

news.headline: Meta’s spending turned its cash flow negative
news.body: Revenue rose 26% to $64.6B, but capex of $34.9B left free cash flow at minus $2.1B, its first cash outflow in over a decade. It guided 2026 capex to $135–145B. Thursday the Nasdaq fell 2.6%, its worst day since June, and the chip index fell 6.7%.

news.headline: Oil hit a six-month high
news.body: Front-month Brent settled at $116.72 Friday and WTI at $103.27, and the energy sector closed at a record. Iran claimed strikes on ships using a US-backed route; Trump called the claims fabricated.

news.headline: Strike talk, but maybe after the midterms
news.body: Trump floated another round of strikes on Iran, then reportedly said any would wait until after Nov 3. Iran says it would reopen Hormuz if the US lifts its naval blockade, and on Sunday its foreign minister said a resumed war would not change its positions.

news.headline: Houthi missiles targeted Saudi Arabia
news.body: Attacks over the weekend aimed at Riyadh, Taif and Yanbu. Riyadh’s airport reopened Sunday after a two-week closure, and the US cut staff at four Middle East embassies.

news.headline: Tesla and SpaceX are studying a merger
news.body: Musk confirmed special committees at both are discussing it, with no deal yet. Tesla’s profit fell 44% to $787M but the stock rose 4.9%; SpaceX reported $4.4B of profit on revenue up 161%.

news.headline: SpaceX’s tower hunt hit telecoms
news.body: Reports that SpaceX sought about 80,000 cell towers for a fourth carrier sent AT&T down 10.7% and T-Mobile down 7.9% on the week. Crown Castle rose 4.5%.

news.headline: Good results, rough reactions
news.body: Lam Research fell 12.8% despite record revenue as its outlook only matched forecasts. GM fell 9.6% despite a beat, higher guidance and a $20B buyback. American Express said it will cut about 5% of staff.

bottom_line.title: Microsoft and Alphabet on Fed day
bottom_line.body: After Meta, investors want to see AI spending covered by cash flow. Big capex raises without the cash to fund them could get the same reaction.

bottom_line.title: The 7,605 line
bottom_line.body: The 100-day average is the floor the index is sitting on. Back above the 50-day near 7,702 would calm things; a close under 7,605 opens 7,564 and then the 200-day near 7,293.

bottom_line.title: Oil and PCE
bottom_line.body: Brent near a six-month high and PCE expected at 3.6% keep December hike odds near 80%. Watch Warsh’s tone Wednesday and the inflation print Thursday.
